title: QuickBooks vs Dolibarr
comparison_markdown:
# QuickBooks vs Dolibarr

## Overview

QuickBooks is the dominant small business accounting platform from Intuit, used by millions of businesses for invoicing, payroll, and tax preparation. Dolibarr is a free open-source ERP and CRM that covers accounting, invoicing, stock management, and customer tracking — replacing both QuickBooks and a basic CRM in a single self-hosted install.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: QuickBooks charges $30-$200+/month; Dolibarr is completely free to self-host
- **Scope**: Dolibarr combines ERP, CRM, and accounting in one tool; QuickBooks is accounting-focused
- **Data ownership**: Dolibarr self-hosted keeps all financial records on your own server
- **Accountant access**: QuickBooks has native accountant collaboration features; Dolibarr requires sharing server access
- **Tax compliance**: QuickBooks has built-in US tax filing integrations; Dolibarr requires manual tax configuration

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | QuickBooks | Dolibarr |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $30-$200+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$1,500/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$6,000/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### QuickBooks

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Dolibarr

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [Dolibarr/dolibarr](https://github.com/Dolibarr/dolibarr) * ~5k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose QuickBooks if:** QuickBooks suits US-based small businesses needing seamless payroll processing, tax preparation, and direct accountant collaboration with minimal setup.

**Choose Dolibarr if:** Dolibarr is ideal for small businesses outside the US, freelancers, or teams wanting to eliminate monthly SaaS fees and manage CRM and accounting in one self-hosted platform.

## Migration Path

Export QuickBooks data via Reports → Export to Excel for your chart of accounts, customer list, and transaction history. Dolibarr supports CSV import for contacts and products. Financial history will need manual entry or accounting journal imports — plan for a clean start-of-year cutover to simplify the transition.

## Our Take

Dolibarr is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid QuickBooks tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Dolibarr instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for QuickBooks, switching to self-hosted Dolibarr will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on QuickBooks until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated QuickBooks paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Dolibarr free to use?
Yes. Dolibarr is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from QuickBooks to Dolibarr?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your QuickBooks data, follow the Dolibarr import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Dolibarr get regular updates?
Yes. Dolibarr has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Dolibarr without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Dolibarr development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [QuickBooks](https://quickbooks.intuit.com) and [Dolibarr](https://dolibarr.org) before making decisions.*

title: Zoho CRM vs Dolibarr
comparison_markdown:
# Zoho CRM vs Dolibarr (2026)

## Overview
Zoho CRM and Dolibarr are customer relationship management (CRM) tools designed to help businesses manage their sales, marketing, and customer service activities. This comparison is beneficial for small to medium-sized businesses and enterprises looking to switch from a proprietary CRM solution to a self-hosted, open-source alternative. The core use case for both tools is to streamline customer interactions, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Zoho CRM offers a subscription-based model, while Dolibarr is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: With Dolibarr, businesses have full ownership and control over their data, whereas Zoho CRM stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Zoho CRM is generally easier to set up and requires less technical expertise, while Dolibarr requires more technical knowledge for self-hosting.
* Scalability: Zoho CRM is more scalable and can handle large volumes of data and users, while Dolibarr's scalability depends on the server infrastructure.
* Integration with Google Drive: Zoho CRM has native integration with Google Drive, while Dolibarr requires a third-party module for similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Zoho CRM | Dolibarr |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $14-$52/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $700-$2,600/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $2,800-$10,400/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Zoho CRM
* Pros:
	+ Easy to set up and use
	+ Scalable and reliable
	+ Native integration with Google Drive
	+ Mobile apps for iOS and Android
	+ 24/5 customer support
* Cons:
	+ Expensive for large teams
	+ Limited customization options
	+ Data storage limits
	+ Dependence on Zoho's servers
### Dolibarr
* Pros:
	+ Free and self-hosted
	+ Full data ownership and control
	+ Customizable and extensible
	+ Community-driven development
	+ Low costs for large teams
* Cons:
	+ Steeper learning curve
	+ Requires technical expertise for self-hosting
	+ Limited mobile support
	+ Dependence on community support
	+ Limited scalability without proper server infrastructure

## When to Choose Each
### Zoho CRM
Zoho CRM is suitable for small to medium-sized businesses that prioritize ease of use, scalability, and reliability. It's ideal for teams that need native integration with Google Drive and require 24/5 customer support. However, for larger teams or businesses with strict data ownership requirements, Zoho CRM may not be the best choice due to its high costs and limited customization options.

### Dolibarr
Dolibarr is a good fit for small to medium-sized businesses that value data ownership, customization, and cost-effectiveness. It's suitable for teams with technical expertise and a willingness to self-host their CRM solution. However, for businesses that require a high level of scalability, reliability, and mobile support, Dolibarr may not be the best choice due to its limitations in these areas.

## Migration Path
1. Export data from Zoho CRM in CSV format.
2. Install and configure Dolibarr on a self-hosted server.
3. Use the Dolibarr import tool to migrate data from the CSV file.
4. Configure user accounts, permissions, and workflows in Dolibarr.
5. Test and verify the migrated data and workflows.

## Our Take
Dolibarr is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited scalability, mobile support, and customer support. While it's a promising open-source CRM solution, it requires significant technical expertise and resources to self-host and customize.

One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching to Dolibarr is its dependence on community support, which can be unpredictable and limited. Additionally, Dolibarr's scalability is heavily dependent on the server infrastructure, which can be a challenge for large teams or businesses with high traffic.

For businesses that value data ownership, customization, and cost-effectiveness, and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and customizing their CRM solution, Dolibarr is a viable alternative to Zoho CRM. However, for teams that prioritize ease of use, scalability, and reliability, Zoho CRM remains a better choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 users that don't need native integration with Google Drive.
* Medium-sized businesses with 10-50 users that require full data ownership and control.
* Enterprises with 50-200 users that are willing to invest in self-hosting and customizing their CRM solution.
* Teams that don't require 24/5 customer support.
* Businesses that prioritize cost-effectiveness and are willing to compromise on scalability and mobile support.

## FAQ
### Can I use Dolibarr for free?
Yes, Dolibarr is free and open-source, and you can self-host it on your own server.

### Is Dolibarr scalable?
Dolibarr's scalability depends on the server infrastructure, and it may not be suitable for large teams or businesses with high traffic.

### Can I integrate Dolibarr with Google Drive?
Yes, Dolibarr has a third-party module for integrating with Google Drive, but it's not native like Zoho CRM.

### Does Dolibarr have mobile apps?
No, Dolibarr has limited mobile support, and it's not as robust as Zoho CRM's mobile apps.

### Can I migrate my data from Zoho CRM to Dolibarr?
Yes, you can export your data from Zoho CRM in CSV format and import it into Dolibarr using its import tool.
